messages:
maria.s: quick heads-up — during the int4 bring-up for gemma-lite we saw consistent quality drops on long-context summarization when input padding length crosses certain boundaries. looks like a head-splitting/padding interaction, not a pure quant noise :thinking:

jake.k: hmm can you paste the minimal repro? is this on gemma conversion pipeline or runtime?

maria.s: runtime. repro is small: run prompt ~1.2k tokens then pad to various multiples until 2k. when pad lands on certain offsets the outputs diverge vs fp16 baseline. short diff sample below.

maria.s: ```
# simplified run
python -m rwinf.eval \\n  --model gemma-lite-int4 \\n  --prompt-file tests/longctx/sample.txt \\n  --pad-to 2048 \\n  --quant int4
```

ashley.t: do you have the pad token id and head-split config? some of our adapters split heads across lanes causing stride mismatches in KV indexing.

maria.s: pad_token=1, head_split=3 (we used a head-splitting transform in quant conversion for better memory packing). config excerpt: 
```yaml
model: gemma-lite
quant: int4
head_split: 3
pad_token_id: 1
kv_layout: headwise-split
```

jake.k: interesting. i remember a qwen onboarding bug where pad aligned with a head-group boundary and we got off-by-one in kvcache offsets. can you dump kvcache keys before/after the boundary? even a small hex dump helps.

maria.s: dumped a quick kvcache trace. around pad offset 1536 (when pad%head_group==0) keys shift by 1 word. small excerpt: 
```
KV[1535] = 0x7f8a22...
KV[1536] = 0x000000... (expected nonzero)
KV[1537] = 0x7f8a22...
```

ashley.t: that smells like our head-split interleaver didn't account for padding sentinel removal when computing virtual_head_index. i can repro locally if you push the converted model and a tiny script.

maria.s: pushed to /tmp/repro_gemmalite_int4.tar.gz and added script tests/eng-ml/headsplit_pad_probe.py. link: https://internal/redwood/tmp/repro_gemmalite_int4 (restricted).

jake.k: quick diff of outputs (pad=1520 vs pad=1536):
- fp16: "Summary: The user reports a minor bug..."
- int4 (pad=1520): "Summary: The user reports a minor bug..."
- int4 (pad=1536): "Summary: The user reports issue with summarization and provides unrelated info about deploys."

maria.s: exact. quality drops only happen at those boundaries, and perplexity spikes ~10-18% on the eval set.

ashley.t: plan: 1) verify layout math in quant conversion for head_split>1; 2) add padding-aware kvcache index unit test; 3) run batch eval across pad ranges to map failure surface. i'll take (1) and (2).

jake.k: assign to ashley.t, add a regression test in rwinf-runtime/tests that iterates pad lengths from 0..2048 step 8 and compares token-by-token to fp16 baseline (with tolerances). logs should capture any pad where token divergence > threshold.

maria.s: added test ticket in phab: T12345 and attached reproducer. also added a short eval table in the ticket showing the spike points.

ci-bot: build queued for branch fix/headsplit-pad-fix (job 9923). :gear:

ashley.t: found the bug — interleaver used floor(head_index/slot_count) but we should use mod arithmetic when pad sentinel collapses lanes. patch incoming, repro now passes local unit test. pushing PR.

jake.k: nice. once CI green, run the full int4 eval (1k prompts) and compare Rouge scores vs fp16 and previous int4. also sanity check qwen/gemma conversion scripts for similar pattern.

maria.s: will run cross-model sweep after merge. quick note to docs: add a one-liner in our conversion README about padding-aware head-splitting.

ashley.t: PR is up: https://internal/redwood/pull/4852 🔁 includes unit test and a small conversion script tweak.

maria.s: thanks. i'll run the sweep and report back. :thumbsup:

jake.k: cool — mark thread resolved when results pass. leaving here for records. :eyes:
